# Isolde Pembroke

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c15 P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022)</sub>
- **Origin:** Pear Hill  <sub>[v1 c2 P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Izzy  <sub>[v3 c29 P10](../source/v03-c29.md#nw-v03-c29-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Isolde is an extremely attractive girl with rosy cheeks, dark eyes, and black hair. Over time, she grows to have dimples and takes on a matronly appearance, while retaining her vibrant black eyes, rosy cheeks, and charming dimples.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v4 c1 P2](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0002)_

## Personality

Isolde possesses a cheerful outlook inherited from her father, along with intelligence and goodness. She is an avid reader who spends much of her time with books. She exhibits a playful and affectionate nature with her close friends, though she occasionally acts out of impatience or teasing.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P22](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0022), [v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052), [v3 c11 P28](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0028)_

## History

Isolde Pembroke grows up at Pear Hill and forms a devoted friendship with Nell Harcourt, sealing a solemn vow of lifelong loyalty over a path pretending it is flowing water. Although their friendship is temporarily banned by her mother after an incident involving raspberry cordial, the misunderstanding is resolved and their bond grows even closer. Together with their peers, they attend school in Brierley, establish play areas like Larkrise, write tales for a story club, and go on visits to her Great-Aunt Lavinia in Port Marlow. As she reaches adulthood, Isolde courts and marries Gideon Duckett, moving to his farm two miles away from Grey Shutters. She subsequently gives birth to two children, including a son and later a daughter named Small Nell Lucinda.

_Sources: [v1 c2 P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c13 P13](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0013), [v1 c16 P42](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0042), [v1 c18 P43](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0043), [v1 c26 P23](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0023), [v1 c29 P17](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0017), [v2 c29 P11](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0011), [v3 c28 P23](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0023), [v3 c29 P11](../source/v03-c29.md#nw-v03-c29-p0011), [v3 c39 P41](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0041), [v4 c1 P2](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0002)_

## Quotes

> A joke is all it is intended to be. And you shouldn't feel so certain that a time will never come when your name is scribbled somewhere. Wilfred Mott is completely infatuated with you. It was to his mother—take note, his mother—that he declared you were the cleverest female student in the whole school. Having that said about you surpasses being attractive.  <sub>[v1 c15 P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022)</sub>

> Aunt Lavinia was the one. Oh, Nell, regardless of how she got to that place, it was Aunt Lavinia. Oh, and her anger is bound to be immense, I am sure. It’s terrible—it truly is terrible—yet Nell, have you ever encountered a thing quite this amusing?  <sub>[v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052)</sub>

> As soon as we begin, our topmost priority should be giving that hall a coat of paint. The sight of it is shameful, so we need to deal with it prior to attempting to make Mr. Levi Boulder demolish his home. Father believes our efforts there are doomed to fail . . . Levi Gammon lacks the generosity to devote the necessary time.  <sub>[v2 c2 P1](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0001)</sub>

> Oh, I was certain it would take the prize—I knew it would. Nell, I submitted your story to the contest.  <sub>[v3 c15 P15](../source/v03-c15.md#nw-v03-c15-p0015)</sub>

> I am so eager for the time when he is big enough to speak. Hearing him call me ‘mother’ is my deepest desire. And oh, I am resolved that he will have a pleasant first recollection of me. My own earliest remembrance of my mother involves her striking me because of an act I had committed. I have no doubt that I merited the punishment, and my mother was invariably wonderful and holds a special place in my heart. Even so, I truly wish that my initial memory concerning her had been more agreeable.  <sub>[v3 c39 P47](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0047)</sub>
